mainTopic: Replacement agents and conditional גיטין; repaying a loan to a כהן, לוי, or עני through their gifts
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. A בית דין may appoint a replacement agent to carry a גט whether or not the first agent is present, and a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל confirms this. Next come two stories of a גט given on a thirty-day condition. In the first, the husband reached the river but could not cross it in time, and שמואל rules that this does not count as coming. In the second, the husband tried to make peace with his wife but she refused. רב יוסף's ruling is reported in two opposite versions, and the גמרא ties them to the question of whether אונס counts in גיטין. A new משנה then lets a lender to a כהן, לוי, or עני repay himself from their gifts, assuming they are still alive. The גמרא brings three answers, from רב, שמואל, and עולא, to how gifts they never received can count as repayment. A ברייתא adds more rules: the cheaper price, no ריבית, no cancellation by שביעית, who may back out, and the case of a loan the lender gave up on. The amud ends with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי אחי on what happens when the borrower dies, and the גמרא asks what difference their two views make. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Must the first agent be present when the court appoints a new one?
steps.stepSummary: The questioner asks whether a בית דין must appoint the new שליח in front of the first agent, or whether it can do so when he is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the בית דין appoints an agent, does it have to be done in front of him, or can it be done when he is not there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the earlier discussion about passing a גט to a new agent and asks a practical question about how the בית דין makes the appointment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new agent gets his power through the בית דין, and that power comes from the first agent. The question is whether this handover has to happen in front of the first agent, or whether the בית דין can do it without him there.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent, here someone who carries the גט
In his presence, in front of him

phrases.english: When the court appoints an agent,
must it be in his presence, or may it be not in his presence?
phrases.notes: "His" means the first agent, the one being replaced.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְשַׁוּוּ בֵּית דִּין שָׁלִיחַ בְּפָנָיו אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about a בית דין appointing a replacement agent for a גט
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the first agent must be present when the בית דין appoints the replacement agent

steps.title: Either way works
steps.stepSummary: The questioner answers his own question: the appointment works whether or not the first agent is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then answered it himself: either in his presence or not in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The same person who asked the question now answers it. The בית דין may appoint the new agent either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The appointment does not depend on the first agent watching it happen. Once the matter is in the hands of the בית דין, they can act even when he is not there.

phrases.english: He then resolved it:
Either in his presence or not in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בית דין may appoint the new agent whether or not the first agent is present

steps.title: A message from ארץ ישראל confirms the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in ארץ ישראל sent the same ruling: either in his presence or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: either in his presence or not in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer with a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer now stands on two supports: the questioner's own conclusion and an independent ruling from the scholars of ארץ ישראל. That makes the הלכה firm.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: A בית דין can appoint a replacement agent for a גט even when the first agent is not present.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Either in his presence or not in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 2
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the appointment works in or out of the first agent's presence
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling sent from the scholars of ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The husband stuck across the river
steps.stepSummary: A husband said the גט takes effect if he does not come within thirty days. He came, but the ferry kept him from crossing, and he shouted, "See that I came!"
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said: If I do not come within thirty days, let this be a גט. He came, but the ferry cut him off. He said to them: "See that I came, see that I came."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a conditional גט. This step only lays out the facts; the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was that the גט takes effect only if he does not come. He made it all the way to the river but could not cross because the ferry was on the other side. So the question is whether getting that close, and calling out, counts as coming.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט, a bill of divorce

phrases.english: A certain man who said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא אָתֵינָא עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין –
phrases.english: If I do not come within thirty days,
let it be a bill of divorce.
He came, and the ferry cut him off.
phrases.notes: The ferry was on the other side of the river, so he could not cross in time.

phrases.english: He said to them: "See that I came, see that I came."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר אִי לָא אָתֵינָא עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a conditional גט that depends on the husband coming
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case; the ruling follows in step 5

steps.title: שמואל: that does not count as coming
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that standing on the other side of the river is not called coming, so the condition was met and the גט takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: That is not called coming.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the ruling on the river story: the husband did not "come," so the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was about actually arriving, not about trying hard or getting close. He was blocked by the river, and his shouting from the far side does not change the fact that he did not arrive. So the condition "if I do not come" was fulfilled and the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not called, it does not count as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the direction. The גט works when he does NOT come. So when שמואל says "this is not coming," he means the גט IS valid.
steps.whatToRemember: In this case, getting close and calling out does not count as arriving. The condition was met, and the גט takes effect.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
That is not called coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר שְׁמוּאֵל לָא שְׁמֵיהּ מַתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case described in step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Being stuck across the river is not considered coming, so the condition is fulfilled and the גט is valid

steps.title: The husband who tried to make peace
steps.stepSummary: A husband said the גט takes effect if he does not make peace with his wife within thirty days. He tried, but she refused to be calmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to them: If I do not make peace with her within thirty days, let this be a גט. He went and tried to make peace with her, but she would not be calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story about a conditional גט. This step lays out the facts, and רב יוסף's ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the condition depends on two people. He did his part by trying, but she did not respond. The question is whether "making peace" means trying, or actually succeeding.

keyTerms.meaning: To make peace with, to calm someone down
She was calmed, she accepted the peacemaking

phrases.english: A certain man who said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" are the agents holding the גט.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא [מְ]פַיֵּיסְנָא לַהּ עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין –
phrases.english: If I do not appease her within thirty days,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: let it be a bill of divorce.
He went and appeased her, but she was not appeased.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ אִי לָא מְפַיֵּיסְנָא לַהּ עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with a similar thirty-day condition, now about making peace
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case; the ruling follows in steps 7 and 8

steps.title: רב יוסף: he did not try hard enough, so the גט works
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks: did he give her a container full of gold coins and she still refused? Since he did not try that hard, he did not really make peace, and the גט takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Did he give her a container full of dinars and she still was not calmed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rules that the husband's effort was not enough, so the condition "if I do not make peace" was met and the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rhetorical question means that a big enough gift would have won her over. Since he did not do that, he did not really make peace with her, and the גט takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A large container or measuring vessel

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Did he give her a vessel full of dinars
and she was not appeased?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מִי יְהַב לַהּ תַּרְקַבָּא דְּדִינָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first version of the ruling on the case in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband did not truly make peace, so the condition was met and the גט is valid

steps.title: Other version: he tried, so the גט does not work
steps.stepSummary: Others report that רב יוסף said the opposite: he did not have to give her a container of gold. He tried, and she refused, so he kept his condition and the גט does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: Did he need to give her a container full of dinars?! He tried to make peace with her, and she was not calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב יוסף's words that reaches the opposite ruling: the husband kept his condition, so there is no divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, "making peace" means making a fair effort, not paying any price it takes. He made the effort, and her refusal is not his fault. So the condition "if I do not make peace" was not met, and the גט does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say, another version of what was said
Is it so? Did he really have to? (a rhetorical opening)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same picture of a container full of dinars, but they reach opposite results. In the first version the גט is valid; in the second it is not.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רב יוסף disagree about what "making peace" means. Version 1 says only real success counts, so the גט works. Version 2 says a fair effort counts, so the גט does not work.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי תַּרְקַבָּא דְּדִינָרֵי בָּעֵי לְמִיתַּב לַהּ?!
phrases.english: Did he need to give her a vessel full of dinars?!
He did appease her, but she was not appeased.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מִידֵּי תַּרְקַבָּא דְּדִינָרֵי בָּעֵי לְמִיתַּב לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רב יוסף's ruling from step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fair effort counts as making peace, so the condition was not met and the גט is not valid
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a condition that depends on another person's response can be read in two ways: by the effort made, or by the result reached.

steps.title: The two versions of רב יוסף depend on whether אונס counts in גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The two reports of רב יוסף reflect a known מחלוקת: does an uncontrollable situation (אונס) count when a גט is on a condition?
steps.simpleTranslation: This version follows the one who says אונס counts in גיטין. That version follows the one who says אונס does not count in גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יוסף was quoted in two opposite ways. Each version matches a different opinion about אונס in a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband tried to make peace, but his wife refused, and he could not control that. If אונס counts, he is not blamed, so the גט does not take effect (the second version). If אונס does not count, all that matters is that peace was not made, so the גט takes effect (the first version).

keyTerms.meaning: a situation beyond a person's control
being forced by circumstances is taken into account for a conditional גט
being forced is not taken into account; only the plain facts matter
according to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רב יוסף are not random. They follow the two sides of the question of whether אונס counts in גיטין.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'הָא' in the line refers to the SECOND version (the גט does not take effect), and the second 'הָא' refers to the FIRST version (the גט takes effect). Don't match them up in the order they were told.

phrases.english: This one is according to the one who says
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the second report, where the husband tried and the גט does not take effect.

phrases.english: there is אונס in bills of divorce,
and that one is according to the one who says
there is no אונס in bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא – כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ אוֹנֶס בְּגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the two opposite reports of רב יוסף in steps 7 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over רב יוסף's view follows the wider מחלוקת of whether אונס counts in גיטין.

steps.title: Lending to a כהן, לוי, or עני and repaying with their gifts
steps.stepSummary: A lender may take the gifts owed to a כהן, לוי, or עני from his produce and count them as repayment of the loan, assuming they are still alive and still eligible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone lends money to a כהן, a לוי, or a poor person, on the understanding that he will set aside their portion and count it against the loan, he may set it aside assuming they are still alive. He does not worry that the כהן or לוי died, or that the poor person became rich.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a loan that gets paid back through the תרומה and מעשרות the lender owes to the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time the lender separates gifts, he keeps them himself and subtracts their value from the debt. The משנה lets him rely on the חזקה that the borrower is still alive and, for the עני, still poor. This continues the earlier theme of assuming a person is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: from their portion, meaning the gifts owed to them
on the assumption that they are still alive

steps.whyThisMatters: This is another case where a person may rely on the חזקה that someone is still alive. That idea connects to the earlier משנה about a גט.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who lends money

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַכֹּהֵן וְאֶת הַלֵּוִי וְאֶת הֶעָנִי,
phrases.english: to a priest, to a Levite, or to a poor person,
so that he will separate against it from their portion;
phrases.notes: He keeps the gifts that belong to them and counts their value as paying back the loan.

phrases.english: he may separate against it on the assumption that they are alive,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא מֵת הַכֹּהֵן אוֹ הַלֵּוִי,
phrases.english: and he need not worry that perhaps the priest or the Levite died,
or that the poor person became rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּלְוֶה מָעוֹת אֶת הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the theme of assuming someone is alive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender may keep separating against the loan, assuming the borrowers are alive and still eligible.

steps.title: If the borrowers died: permission from the heirs
steps.stepSummary: If the borrowers died, the lender needs the heirs' permission to continue. If the loan was made before a בית דין, he does not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they died, he must get permission from the heirs. If he lent to them in front of a בית דין, he does not need permission from the heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case, where the borrower is known to have died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower dies, the arrangement normally needs the heirs' agreement. A loan made in front of a בית דין is the exception: it stays in force without asking the heirs.

phrases.aramaic: מֵתוּ – צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁים;
phrases.english: If they died, he must get permission from the heirs;
if he lent to them in front of a court,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין.
phrases.english: he does not need to get permission from the heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתוּ – צָרִיךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case where the borrowers are known to have died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the borrowers died, the lender needs the heirs' permission, unless the loan was made in front of a בית דין.

steps.title: How can gifts they never received pay off their loan?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the כהן, לוי, or עני never actually received these gifts, so how can those gifts count as their repayment?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does this work even though the gifts never came into their hands?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a challenge to the משנה's arrangement. This sets up the answer that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying back a loan with the gifts means the gifts first belong to the borrower and then pass to the lender. But the gifts never reached the borrower's hands. So how can he own them and hand them over?

keyTerms.meaning: they did not come into his hand (his possession)

phrases.english: GEMARA: And even though
they never came into his hand?!
phrases.notes: 'They' are the תרומה and מעשרות, which never reached the כהן, לוי, or עני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָתוּ לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic arrangement of the משנה in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the separated gifts count as repayment of the loan.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot pass along something that never came into his possession, and the borrowers never received these gifts.

steps.title: רב: the case is about the regular associates of a כהן or לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה is talking about a כהן or לוי who has a fixed arrangement with this farmer, so he already counts as owning the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The משנה is talking about the regular associates of the כהונה and the לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer to the challenge of Step 12. He explains how the כהן or לוי can be repaid with gifts he never received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the כהן or לוי never owned these gifts. רב answers that this particular כהן or לוי always gets this farmer's gifts. Because of that set arrangement, the gifts already count as his, so they can be used to pay off his loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular associates of a כהן: people who always give their gifts to the same כהן
The status of being a לוי, here the לוי who receives מעשר

phrases.english: Rav said:
It is about the regular associates of the priesthood and the Levites.
phrases.notes: He means a farmer who always gives his gifts to this same כהן or לוי, so they are already as good as his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בְּמַכָּרֵי כְּהוּנָּה וּלְוִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a set arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן or לוי never owned the gifts, so they cannot repay his loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the fixed arrangement, this כהן or לוי counts as already owning the gifts.

steps.title: שמואל: someone else acquired the gifts for them
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the farmer had another person acquire the gifts on behalf of the כהן, לוי, or עני, so they truly own them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The case is where he gives them ownership through other people.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the gifts really did become theirs, because a third person acquired the gifts on their behalf. After that, the lender can take those gifts back as payment of their debt.

keyTerms.meaning: Through other people who acquire on his behalf

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
It is where he gives them ownership through others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בִּמְזַכֶּה לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to one where a real acquisition happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one ever acquired the gifts for the כהן, לוי, or עני.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another person acquired the gifts for them, so the gifts really became theirs.

steps.title: עולא: the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds that the חכמים treated someone who did not acquire as if he did acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יוסי, who said: They made one who does not acquire like one who acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a third answer. He does not narrow the case. Instead, he says which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, there is no real acquisition here at all. The חכמים made a special rule that treats the כהן, לוי, or עני as if he acquired the gifts. That rule follows רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים treated someone who did not acquire as if he acquired

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: עָשׂוּ אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה.
phrases.english: who said: They made one who does not acquire like one who acquires.
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים, who set up this rule themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer that works differently. It identifies the תנא instead of narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to one תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a real acquisition, the gifts cannot count as theirs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יוסי, the חכמים treated it as an acquisition even without one.

steps.title: Why each אמורא does not accept the other answers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why each אמורא rejects the others. רב's case and שמואל's case are not written in the משנה. עולא's answer makes the משנה follow a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The others do not say like רב, because the משנה does not mention associates. They do not say like שמואל, because the משנה does not mention giving ownership through others. They also do not say like עולא, because we do not explain a משנה as following a lone opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the three אמוראים did not simply agree with each other. It points out the weak spot in each answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל each add a detail to the case that the משנה never mentions, and that is the problem with both of them. עולא avoids adding details, but he makes the משנה follow רבי יוסי, who is one person against the majority. The גמרא avoids explaining a משנה that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה does not teach this
A lone opinion, held by one person against the majority
We do not set up (explain) the משנה this way

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of all three answers. Each answer still stands. The גמרא is only explaining why each אמורא chose his own answer over the others.

phrases.english: All of them do not say like Rav –
phrases.notes: "All of them" here means the other two, שמואל and עולא.

phrases.english: it does not teach "associates."
They do not say like Shmuel –
it does not teach "giving ownership."
They also do not say like Ulla –
we do not set it up according to a lone opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ כְּרַב לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the three answers and shows the weakness of each.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Each answer is rejected only by the other אמוראים, not by the גמרא as a whole.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב and שמואל add details the משנה does not mention. עולא makes the משנה follow a lone opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers. רב says it is a set arrangement. שמואל says someone acquired the gifts for them. עולא says it follows רבי יוסי. Each has a weak point: the first two are not written in the משנה, and the third follows a lone opinion.

steps.title: ברייתא: the lender may separate gifts while the borrowers are presumed alive
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who lent money to a כהן, לוי, or עני, planning to separate their gifts against the loan, may do so on the assumption that they are still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If someone lends money to a כהן, a לוי, or an עני, so that he can separate their portion against the loan, he may separate against it, assuming they are still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the same loan arrangement. It opens a new section with more rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender does not have to check before each separation whether the borrower is still alive. He may assume the borrower is still alive (a חזקה), and count the gifts toward the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Their portion: the gifts that belong to them
On the assumption that they are still alive

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who lends money to the priest,
or to the Levite, or to the poor person,
in order to separate their portion against it,
phrases.notes: "Against it" means against the money of the loan, so each separation pays back part of the debt.

phrases.english: he may separate against it
on the assumption that they are alive;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּלְוֶה מָעוֹת אֶת הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that expands on the arrangement in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender may keep separating gifts against the loan, assuming the borrowers are still alive.

steps.title: ברייתא continues: cheaper rate, no ריבית, not canceled by שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds three rules. The lender may fix the price at the cheaper rate. This does not count as ריבית. And שביעית does not cancel this loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may set the price with them at the cheaper rate. It is not considered ריבית. And שביעית does not cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with three more rules about this loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender may count the gifts at whichever price is lower, the price at the time of the loan or at the time he separates. Even if that means he takes back more produce, it is not forbidden ריבית. Also, the loan stays in force after שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The שביעית year cancels the debt

steps.whyThisMatters: These rules show that this loan is treated differently from an ordinary loan. Both ריבית and שמיטת כספים would normally apply to a loan, but here they do not.

phrases.english: And he may set a price with them at the cheap rate;
phrases.notes: He may use the lower price, either from when he gave the loan or from when he separates.

phrases.english: and it is not subject to the prohibition of interest;
and the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it;

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפוֹסֵק עִמָּהֶן כְּשַׁעַר הַזּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender may fix the price at the cheaper rate. This is not ריבית, and שביעית does not cancel the loan.

steps.title: The lender cannot back out, and a loan he gave up on cannot be used
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with two rules. Once the lender has made this arrangement, he cannot back out. If he gave up hope of the money, he can no longer separate the gifts against it, because one does not separate against something lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he wants to back out, he cannot back out. If the owner gave up hope, he does not separate against that money, because we do not separate against something that is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from steps 17-18 continues with its last two rules. The first is that the deal is binding. The second is that the deal ends once the lender gives up hope of the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender locked himself into this deal, so he cannot change his mind. But once he gives up hope of being repaid, the money is treated as gone. You cannot use gone money as the basis for separating gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: Backs out, takes back what he agreed to
Separates the gifts (תרומה, מעשר) from the produce

phrases.english: And if he comes to back out, he cannot back out.
If the owners gave up hope,
phrases.notes: The 'owner' here is the lender, who gave up on ever getting this money back.

phrases.english: he does not separate the gifts against that money,
because we do not separate against something lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּא לַחֲזוֹר – אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 17-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrangement cannot be cancelled by the lender. Once he gives up hope of the money, he may no longer separate the gifts against it.

steps.title: Isn't the cheap-price rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that the lender may fix the price at the cheaper rate. It asks why this needs to be said, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He may set the price with them at the cheap rate. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to explain the ברייתא's rules one by one. It starts with the cheap-price rule and asks why it even needs to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two sides agreed on the cheap price, of course the lender may use it. So the ברייתא seems to be teaching nothing new. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' — the גמרא quoting a line from a source to discuss it

phrases.english: The Master said:
He may set the price with them at the cheap rate.
That's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to explain a rule from the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line פוסק עמהם כשער הזול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the price was agreed on, the lender obviously may use it, so the line seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The cheap price applies even without saying so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא teaches something new. Even if the lender never actually set the price, he is treated as if he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: even though he did not set the price, it is as if he set it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question. The new point is that no spoken agreement about the price is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about a case where they agreed out loud. Even when nothing was said, the lender gets the cheap price automatically, as if they had agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us (the new point)
It is as if he set the price

steps.whatToRemember: The lender gets the cheap price even without agreeing to it out loud.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
even though he did not set the price,
it is as if he set it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the rule applies even with no spoken agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about a case where they agreed on the cheap price, which would be obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without any agreement, the lender is treated as if he set the cheap price.

steps.title: Why is this not ריבית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that this deal is not ריבית. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it is not considered ריבית' — what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule of the ברייתא and asks why it is true. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting the produce at the cheap price means the lender gets back more value than he lent. Normally that would look like ריבית, so the גמרא wants to know why it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest, which is forbidden between Jews

phrases.english: 'And it is not considered interest' —
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second rule from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why getting the produce at the cheap price is not forbidden interest.

steps.title: Not a real loan, so not ריבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that when there is no produce, the borrower pays nothing. Since repayment depends on having produce, it is not a normal loan, so it is not ריבית even when there is produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since when he has nothing, he does not give him anything, then also when he has, it is not considered interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ריבית question. The loan is repaid only if there is produce, so it is not a normal loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבית, the borrower must pay back no matter what. Here the borrower pays nothing if there is no produce, so the lender takes a real risk. That is why getting a good price when there is produce is not counted as interest.

phrases.english: Since when he has nothing,
phrases.notes: This means when there is no produce to give the gifts from, for example after a drought.

phrases.english: he does not give him anything,
then also when he has,
it is not considered interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי לֵית לֵיהּ – לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Repayment depends on whether there is produce, so it is not a guaranteed loan and therefore not ריבית.

steps.title: Why שביעית does not cancel this loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the last rule. שביעית does not cancel this loan because the פסוק 'לא יגוש' (he shall not demand) does not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And שביעית does not cancel it' — because we cannot apply to it the words 'he shall not demand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's last rule. It shows why שביעית has no effect on this kind of loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביעית cancels loans by forbidding the lender to demand payment. This lender could never demand payment anyway, since he can only take back the gifts. So the פסוק does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, which cancels debts
We can apply the פסוק to it

steps.whatToRemember: All three rules come from one idea. This is not a normal loan: there is no guaranteed repayment and no right to demand payment.

phrases.english: 'And the seventh year does not cancel it' —
because we cannot apply to it 'he shall not demand.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:2

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ לֹא יִגּוֹשׂ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third rule from step 18, following the explanation of the ריבית rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שביעית cancels only loans that the lender could demand. This loan could never be demanded, so the פסוק לא יגוש does not apply.

steps.title: Only the homeowner is locked into the deal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that someone who tries to back out cannot. רב פפא limits this: it applies only to the בעל הבית backing out against the כהן. A כהן who wants to back out may do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'If he wants to back out, he can't.' רב פפא said: That was only taught about a homeowner backing out on a כהן. But a כהן backing out on a homeowner may back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. רב פפא then explains that the rule only works in one direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'he cannot back out' sounds like it binds both sides. רב פפא says it binds only the בעל הבית, who must keep collecting his loan through the gifts and cannot demand cash back. The כהן keeps the right to cancel. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: to back out, to go back on a deal
homeowner; here, the lender who owns the produce
they only taught this about..., a phrase that limits a rule

phrases.english: And if he seeks to back out, he cannot back out.
Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בְּכֹהֵן;
phrases.english: They only taught this about a homeowner backing out against a priest;
but a priest against a homeowner,
if he seeks to back out, he may back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the בעל הבית cannot back out. The כהן may back out.

steps.title: Proof: money without pulling lets the seller back out
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's ruling is supported by a משנה. When a buyer has paid money but has not yet pulled the produce, the deal is not final and it can still be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he gave him money but did not pull the produce from him, he can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show why the כהן is allowed to back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the standard rule, paying money alone does not finalize a sale of produce. Pulling the produce does. Here the כהן took money, but the בעל הבית never pulled any produce, so the כהן is like a seller who can still cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
pulled, the act of taking hold that finalizes buying movable things

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: בבא מציעא 44a.

phrases.english: If he gave him money
but did not pull produce from him,
he can back out of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נָתַן לוֹ מָעוֹת וְלֹא מָשַׁךְ הֵימֶנּוּ פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב פפא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן may back out of the deal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that paying money without pulling the produce does not finalize a sale.
steps.whatToRemember: In this deal, the בעל הבית is bound, but the כהן can still cancel, because money alone does not finalize a sale of produce.

steps.title: Why say he cannot separate on a lost loan?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if the owner has given up hope of getting the loan back, he cannot separate gifts against it, because one does not separate on something lost. The גמרא asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: If the owner gave up hope, he does not separate on that money, because one does not separate on what is lost. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and challenges it as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the lender has given up on the money, nothing is left to collect. So of course he cannot keep paying himself back through the gifts. The גמרא wants to know what the ברייתא adds by spelling this out.

keyTerms.meaning: separates gifts such as תרומה and מעשר

phrases.english: If the owners gave up hope,
phrases.notes: This means the lender, who has given up on ever getting this loan back.

phrases.english: he does not separate on the basis of that money,
because one does not separate on what is lost.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא and attacks it as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line about a loan the owner has given up on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A loan the owner has given up on is clearly gone, so stating the rule seems pointless.

steps.title: Needed for crops that sprouted dry stalks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule is needed for a case where the crops sprouted stalks and dried out. You might think the stalks leave some real hope. The ברייתא teaches that the owner still counts as having given up.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where they sprouted stalks. You might have said that sprouting stalks is something significant. So it teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a borderline case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the crops had simply been destroyed, giving up hope would be obvious. When they have sprouted stalks, one could think there is still a real chance they will recover. The ברייתא teaches that this hope does not count, so he cannot separate on that money.

keyTerms.meaning: no, it is needed for a specific case

phrases.english: No, it is needed where they sprouted stalks;
phrases.notes: Picture crops that came up as stalks and then dried out, so recovery is very unlikely.

phrases.english: you might have said
that sprouting stalks is something significant,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּאֲקוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a specific case where the rule teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the crops sprouted stalks, there is still real hope, so the owner has not truly given up.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with stalks, the owner counts as having given up, so he cannot separate on that money.

steps.title: When the borrower dies, keep separating for the group
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that if the כהן or לוי who borrowed in court dies, the lender keeps separating as if for that tribe. If a poor borrower dies, the lender keeps separating as if for the poor of ישראל. רבי אחי says 'the poor of the world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: If someone lent money in court to a כהן or a לוי and they died, he keeps separating against the loan on the presumption of that tribe. If he lent to a poor man in court and he died, he keeps separating on the presumption of the poor of ישראל. רבי אחי says: on the presumption of the poor of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about what happens to the deal when the borrower dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death of the borrower does not end the arrangement. The lender can keep separating gifts against the loan, assuming that the tribe of the dead כהן or לוי, or the poor, will take the borrower's place. For the poor man's case, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says 'poor of ישראל' and רבי אחי says 'poor of the world.' What practical difference this makes is the question of the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּלְוֶה מָעוֹת אֶת הַכֹּהֵן וְאֶת הַלֵּוִי בְּבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: One who lends money to a priest or to a Levite in court,
and they died,
he separates on the basis of that money
on the presumption of that tribe.
phrases.notes: He assumes someone from the borrower's tribe stands in his place, so the arrangement carries on.

phrases.english: And if he lent to a poor man in court, and he died,
he separates on the basis of that money
on the presumption of the poor of Israel.
Rabbi Aḥai says:
On the presumption of the poor of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's clause in step 11 about a loan made in front of a בית דין when the borrower died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrangement continues after the borrower's death, with the borrower's tribe, or the poor, standing in his place.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the deal is tied to the group the gifts belong to, not only to the one person who borrowed.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the practical difference is between 'poor of ישראל' and 'poor of the world.' It seems that רבי אחי must also mean only Jewish poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two opinions disagree about in practice. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gifts like מעשר עני go only to Jewish poor people. So even 'poor of the world' cannot include non-Jews, and the two wordings look the same. The גמרא wants to find the real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי אחי as including non-Jewish poor. Both opinions are about Jewish poor people, which is exactly why the גמרא asks what the difference is.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the disagreement in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between 'poor of ישראל' and 'poor of the world.'
